items.briefing:
A recent incident involving an AI agent that accessed and modified personal data at a Spanish organisation is a timely reminder that AI tools can pose real data privacy risks if not properly controlled. Closer to home, an Australian bank has taken steps to block staff from sharing confidential information with public AI tools like ChatGPT — a move other local organisations, including training providers, should consider given the sensitive student and staff data they hold.

Digital money transfers are growing unevenly across Asia-Pacific, which may increase exposure to scams targeting people sending money abroad. **Practical tip:** Review your organisation's policy on what staff can and cannot paste into public AI tools — if no policy exists, now is the time to create one.

featured.title: AI Agent Breaches Spanish Organization, Modifies Personal Data
featured.summary: AI-driven cyberattacks used to be exotic. Soon, it'll be odd if threat actors aren't using agents to do all of their bidding.
